title: Pointwise update of an induced tape
statement: Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $F$ assign a block of $N+1$ optional bits to each integer, and choose $z\in\mathbb{Z}$, $j\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$, and an optional bit $b$. Updating the induced tape at position $(N+1)z+j$ to $b$ gives the tape induced by the family obtained from $F$ by replacing entry $j$ of block $z$ by $b$ and leaving every other entry unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ assigns a block of $N+1$ optional bits to each integer
replaced:
Let $F$ assign to every integer a block of $N+1$ optional bits, let $z \in \mathbb{Z}$,
$j \in \{0,\dots,N\}$, and let $b$ be an optional bit. Overwriting the binary tape
induced by $F$ at position $(N+1)z + j$ with the value $b$ yields the binary tape
induced by the family that agrees with $F$ everywhere except that entry $j$ of block
$z$ becomes $b$.
